chunks: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you falls ill, let him give permission to the people to come to him, for there is no one except that he has an answered supplication.'

key_terms.دَعْوَةٌ مُسْتَجَابَةٌ: An answered/accepted supplication — a prayer that God has guaranteed to accept
key_terms.فَلْيَأْذَنْ: Let him give permission — an imperative indicating strong recommendation or obligation

ai.seo_question: Why should a sick person allow visitors according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: Imam Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) instructs that when a person falls ill, he should permit people to visit him. The theological reasoning given is profound: every person carries within him an answered supplication (da'wa mustajaba), and by allowing visitors, the sick person can benefit from their prayers on his behalf. This teaching reflects the early Muslim community's understanding that illness is a communal matter, and the intercessory prayers of visitors hold special spiritual value.
